headline: Highest risk is low: no shared I/O or network surfaces are documented, so prompt injection, leakage, and cascading failure pathways are not evidenced for this pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface is documented for botpress or data-engineering-zoomcamp. Both profiles show io_surfaces as empty and network_egress as none, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because the pairwise pathway is absent in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared clipboard, filesystem, or message queue, reassess injection risk.
IF an MCP or other shared tool channel is added, the pathway may become non-none.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated from shared copy-paste workflows.
Do not connect either agent to a shared workspace without provenance controls.
requires-engineering: add explicit input provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither botpress nor data-engineering-zoomcamp documents a shared workspace, sensitive data class, or outbound network path. With network_egress set to none for both and data_classes_touched empty, there is no documented route for one agent to leak the other's data. The pairwise leakage pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is given access to a shared filesystem containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either profile later gains network egress, re-evaluate exfiltration pathways.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files off any shared directory.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation if shared storage is needed.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces, mutable resources, or concurrency primitives. botpress only lists install_packages and no write target; data-engineering-zoomcamp lists no write capability at all. Without a shared mutable surface, capability conflict is not plausible from the documented profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk becomes relevant.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents write access to the same path.
Keep repository state read-only for the course agent.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if shared mutable state is added.

D_cascading_error.rationale: No evidence shows that data-engineering-zoomcamp consumes botpress outputs as authoritative, and neither profile documents downstream action-taking authority. botpress is a customer-support agent, while data-engineering-zoomcamp is a course-like data-engineering asset; the profiles do not establish an output-to-action chain. The cascading-error pathway is not documented.
conditions: IF botpress outputs are wired directly into the other agent's decision path, reassess.
IF either agent is given authority to send emails, commit code, or trigger jobs, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any downstream action.
Do not auto-feed one agent's text into the other as instructions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates for any future action pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either botpress or data-engineering-zoomcamp. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair. The other agent is not cited separately because no compliance-sensitive flow is established.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, reassess compliance obligations.
IF deployment documentation later specifies residency or retention constraints, re-evaluate.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair's workflow.
Document any future residency or retention requirements before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy checks if regulated data is introduced.
